name: mc_build
title: Build
description:
Places blocks in the Minecraft world in bulk: cuboid fills, individual block placements, and/or lettering rendered by the plugin (`text`), up to 500,000 blocks per call. Executes asynchronously across ticks, so large builds do not lag players.

WHEN TO USE: build a saved reusable design with `blueprint:{id:...,palette:{...}}` (managed by mc_blueprint), or any task placing more than a handful of blocks - buildings, terrain shaping, clearing space, roads, walls. Prefer few large `fills`. Use `blocks` for details needing a specific orientation or state (stairs, doors, torches, signs): pass the full block state string, e.g. `minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=north,half=bottom]`. Use `text` for lettering bigger than a single sign - never place letter-shaped blocks by hand.
WHEN NOT TO USE: to read the world (use `mc_survey`/`mc_inspect`); to run a server command (use `mc_command`).

COORDINATES: A `blueprint` selector cannot be combined with direct fills/blocks/text. Its component mirrors/rotations are applied first, then instance positions and project-frame repetition, then the project `transform`. All components compile into the existing global fills -> text -> blocks passes, preserving instance order within each pass; a snapshot captures their union once. Dimensions/constraints are advisory. X grows east, Z grows south, Y grows up. Coordinates are absolute unless `transform` is supplied: then every fill corner, block position and text position is local to `transform.origin`. Mirror local X or Z first, rotate clockwise viewed from above, then add the world origin. Block states (including omitted defaults), filter orientations and expanded text geometry transform with the positions; sign strings stay readable, but mirrored block lettering has mirrored glyphs. Supply both halves of doors/beds yourself. `from`/`to` are inclusive corners in any order. Volume = (x2-x1+1)*(y2-y1+1)*(z2-z1+1). Operations run in array order - put clearing (`minecraft:air`) before filling. `mode`: "replace" (default) overwrites everything; "keep" fills only air; "outline"/"hollow" place a 1-block shell (hollow also clears the inside); "walls" places only the four vertical sides - use it for rooms, then add a floor and roof separately. `filter` restricts a fill to blocks matching that state (e.g. `filter: "minecraft:air"` builds only into empty space). Blocks are placed without physics by default (sand/gravel do not fall; water/lava sit frozen); `liquids: "flow"` makes water/lava spread and fall normally. Connectable blocks (panes, fences, walls, bars, stairs) get a shape-only update so they connect like hand-placed blocks. To write a sign, pass a `sign` object on a `blocks` entry whose block is a sign, e.g. `minecraft:oak_wall_sign[facing=south]` in the air block in front of the wall - never replace the wall block itself.

SIDE EFFECTS: dryRun:true returns read-only site diagnostics without snapshots or writes; use mc_plan for image previews. Otherwise permanently modifies the world. Every phase is structurally validated before the first snapshot/write, including aggregate limits and sign data. Optional preflight:true also rejects pairing/support failures or incomplete neighbor checks before writing; overwritten non-air cells remain advisory, since terrain cannot be distinguished from structures. Site checks do not reserve the world or simulate connections, fluid spreading or entities. Set `snapshot: true` to save the affected region first, so `mc_restore` can undo this call. Limits per call: 500,000 blocks total, 1,024 chunks footprint, one world (see `liquids` for its own, smaller cap); an over-limit request is rejected before anything changes. The response lists WARNINGS for unsupported blocks (ladders, torches, signs, doors, carpets...); fix those before reporting the build done.

dryRun.description: Read-only final-scene analysis; no snapshots or writes. Returns a JSON report. Use mc_plan for images.

preflight.description: Before building, check the final virtual site and reject missing/incompatible door/bed parts, support warnings or incomplete neighbor checking. Collision/overlap counts are advisory. Structural validation always runs regardless of this flag.

world.description: World name. Omitted uses the plugin's configured default world.

blueprint.description: Build a saved mc_blueprint document. Exclusive with direct fills/blocks/text. Optional palette overrides document bindings; instance bindings take precedence. Compiled states are validated before snapshots/writes; expansion and aggregate server limits apply.

palette.description: Role name -> literal block state. Component defaults < document palette < these overrides < instance palette. Inline properties on $role[property=value] override bound properties.

transform.description: Optional local coordinate frame for ALL fills, blocks and text. Mirror first, rotate second, translate last. Omit to preserve existing absolute-coordinate behavior. Rotation is clockwise viewed from above: 90 maps local east (+X) to world south (+Z). No automatic paired-block creation.

origin.description: World [x,y,z] location of local [0,0,0]. Required when transform is present; coordinates must be signed 32-bit integers.

rotation.description: Clockwise degrees around local Y, viewed from above. Default 0.

mirror.description: Local coordinate to negate before rotation: x reflects across the YZ plane; z reflects across the XY plane. Default none. Does not flip Y.

fills.description: Cuboid fill operations, executed in array order via the plugin's fill_batch RPC.

to.description: Inclusive [x, y, z] corner opposite `from`. Order does not matter.

block.description: Block state string in the "minecraft:" namespace, optionally with properties, e.g. "minecraft:stone" or "minecraft:oak_log[axis=y]". Attached/oriented blocks (ladders, torches, signs, doors, stairs): see the orientation rules on `blocks[].block`; the same rules apply here.

mode.description: "replace" (default) overwrites everything; "keep" only fills air; "outline" places only the 1-block shell on all six faces; "hollow" places that shell and clears the inside; "walls" places only the four vertical sides (no floor or ceiling) and leaves the inside untouched - use "walls" for rooms and buildings, then add a floor and a roof with separate fills. On natural terrain, clear the interior with an "air" fill first: "walls" does not remove grass, flowers, snow or dirt inside.

filter.description: Only replace cells whose current block matches this state string (unspecified properties act as a wildcard), e.g. "minecraft:air" to build only into empty space - useful for repairing a crater or hole without disturbing the surrounding undamaged terrain: fill the bounding box with `filter: "minecraft:air"` so only the missing air pockets are replaced.

blocks.description: Individual block placements, executed in array order via the plugin's set_blocks RPC.

pos.description: [x, y, z] position: absolute by default, local when transform is supplied.

block.description: Block state string in the "minecraft:" namespace, with properties for orientation where relevant, e.g. "minecraft:oak_stairs[facing=north,half=bottom]". Orientation rules: for attached blocks (ladder, wall_torch, wall_sign, wall_banner, lever/button with face=wall) `facing` points AWAY from the supporting block - a ladder on the west wall of a room is ladder[facing=east]. Doors: the panel sits flush with the block face OPPOSITE to `facing`, so a door in a south wall that should be flush with the outside uses facing=north; place half=lower at y and half=upper at y+1 with identical other properties; hinge=left/right chooses the swing side. Stairs: the tall half is on the `facing` side (you walk up toward `facing`); half=top for upside-down stairs. Beds: part=foot at pos, part=head one block toward `facing`. Chests/furnaces: `facing` is the side the front is on. Slabs: type=bottom|top|double. Torches: `torch` stands on a solid block below; a torch on a wall is `wall_torch[facing=<away from the wall>]` placed in the air block beside the wall - never replace a wall block with a torch. Same for `soul_torch`/`redstone_torch`. Chests: with connect enabled, adjacent single chests with the same facing are paired automatically - normally write `type=single` (or omit `type`) and the same `facing` for both halves. For advanced static exact-state plans with connect:false, provide consistent explicit type=left/right halves; verify both types and positions, never guess handedness. Exact verification includes chest type.

sign.description: Sign text/appearance to write onto this entry's block, which must be a sign (block name ending in "_sign" or "_hanging_sign"). At least one of front/back must be given.

front.description: Up to 4 lines of text for the sign's front side, top to bottom. Missing lines are left blank. Each line max 64 characters.

back.description: Up to 4 lines of text for the sign's back side, top to bottom. Missing lines are left blank. Each line max 64 characters.

color.description: Dye color name for the text, e.g. "black" (default) or "red". Applies to whichever of front/back is given.

glowing.description: Whether the text has the glow-ink-sac glowing effect. Default false.

waxed.description: Whether the sign is waxed (can no longer be edited by right-clicking with a dye). Default false.

text.description: Renders lettering as blocks: the plugin's built-in 5x7 dot-matrix font for ASCII, or java.awt for non-ASCII (CJK etc.: 12 rows tall, up to 12 columns per character; a line mixing both is 12 rows, everything sitting on one baseline). Use this for any name, label or word made of blocks (a name over a gate, "WELCOME" on a hillside, a shop sign bigger than a single sign block) instead of placing letter-shaped blocks yourself - hand-placed letters come out misshapen; this does not. Executed via the same fill_batch machinery as `fills` (one run per row of pixels, not one block at a time), so it counts against the same 500,000-block/1,024-chunk limits and gets the same connect/support-warning handling.

The text to render, 1-64 characters after trimming. Up to 4 lines separated by \n; each new line starts one row below the previous, with a 1-row gap. Printable ASCII uses the built-in 5x7 font; any other character (CJK etc.) is rendered through this server's Java font rendering and fails the whole call with a clear error if this JVM has no fonts for it - retry with ASCII text instead.

pos.description: The [x, y, z] block of the first (top) line of text, in the viewer's frame - see `facing`. With `align: "left"` (default) this is the bottom-left pixel; with `align: "center"` it is the bottom-CENTRE (see `align`). For a wall-mounted `facing: "south"/"north"/"east"/"west"` text this is a block in the wall's own plane (the text is one block thick); for `facing: "up"` it is a block on the ground the text lies flat on.

block.description: Block state string for the letters themselves, e.g. "minecraft:white_concrete". Solid, opaque blocks read best; avoid transparent/see-through blocks unless a see-through sign effect is wanted.

align.description: How `pos` relates to the text, along the advance (reading) axis. "left" (default): `pos` is the bottom-left block of the first line. "center": `pos` is the bottom-CENTRE block of the first line - the text extends half its total width to each side of `pos`; when the width does not split evenly, the extra block goes on the advance-positive side (the side the text continues onto). Use "center" for free-standing lettering anchored on a player's position, so no manual half-width math is needed.

background.description: Optional block state string for a solid plaque behind the letters, covering the text's full bounding box (not just the ink). Omit for no background - then only the ink is written and the gaps between/around letters are left completely untouched (no air is written into them), so text can be painted directly onto an existing wall without disturbing it.

facing.description: Which direction the text reads from. "south" (default): upright, readable by someone standing south of it looking north. "north"/"east"/"west": upright, readable from that side. "up": flat on the ground (the y = pos.y plane), readable from above, with the top of the letters toward north - use this for a word on a floor, path or platform.

scale.description: Each font pixel becomes an NxN block square, N = this value. Default 1 (a capital letter is 5x7 blocks, a CJK character about 12x12). Use 2-4 for lettering meant to be read from a distance (a hillside or a large building facade).

spacing.description: Columns of blank space between adjacent glyphs, before `scale` is applied. Default 1.

snapshot.description: When true, snapshot the bounding box of all fills/blocks before building, so mc_restore can undo this call. Default: false.

connect.description: Whether connectable blocks (glass panes, fences, walls, iron bars, stairs, redstone wire) get a shape-only update after placing so they connect to their neighbours. Default: true. Set false to skip this pass (e.g. for speed on a very large batch, or to intentionally leave a disconnected placeholder shape).

liquids.description: "static" (default) places water/lava as a frozen still block, exactly as before - it never flows or drains, useful for a pond, pool or lava lake that should stay put. "flow" places water/lava with real physics: a single water/lava source block placed with `liquids: "flow"` spreads and falls like a hand-placed one, so a fountain (source at the top, open air below, a basin to catch it), a waterfall (source at a cliff edge) or a stream (source at the high end of a sloped channel) actually flows. Applies to every `minecraft:water`/`minecraft:lava` target in this call's `fills` and `blocks`, not just one; every other block is unaffected either way. Capped separately from the overall block limit - a large `flow` fill (e.g. filling a whole lake with source blocks) can be rejected even when well under 500,000 blocks, so use `flow` for a small number of source blocks, not to bulk-fill a liquid body.
